question: Some people think that newspapers are the best way to learn about the news. However, others believe that they can learn about the news better through other media. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

It's better to avoid stereotypical introductions like yours. The introduction
should do two jobs. After reading it, the examiner should know
• what the question is
• what you position is
See my posts on introductions for a simple and effective way of quickly
writing an introduction here. With you level of grammar, you could easily
write an opinions are divided introduction.
You have addressed all parts of the question.
• addresses all parts of the task
Band score 7 TR
Your position
is only revealed in the conclusion, and it would be quite easy to mention
it elsewhere.
Some arguments are weak, especially the one about disabled people.
I would not introduce new ideas in the conclusion.
Neither paragraph has any indication that it has your support. Using Some
argue that could suggest that you don't share that view, but for this to
work, you need to use However, the fact is that or a similar structure in
main body paragraph 2. For a 7, you'd need to make your position clearer
throughout.
Your ideas are but not always clear — see the phrases in bold.
By focusing on convenience, you avoided the question of which option
provides better information. As you focused on convenience, you could
also mention cost — it's free once you're connected. That would be a
better argument than the one about disabled people, You could also
conclude that new media are better for people who have the technology
— ie most people — but for older people, [...l
